## Summary

Distinguish between 'Travel' and 'Lift', noting that T-swapping the front is required for over roughly 9-10.5 inches of total travel. [t553]

Identify Articulation as the difference in wheel height between two points. [t553]

[Partial] Measure Clearance from ground to the lowest underside point, noting tire sizes of 33s or 35s. [t553]

[Partial] Define Droop as the amount a tire sags from its normal full-weight position. [t553]

[Partial] Determine OE width via bumper fitment, then install bumpers and winches before fine-tuning shocks. [t553]

## Specifications

- **Front suspension travel limit**: 9 inches [t553] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)
- **Minimum recommended droop**: 2 to 2.5 inches [t553] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Single wheel articulation lift**: 22 inches [t553] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Tire size for increased clearance**: 33s or 35s [t553] ([Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- Note that T-swapping the front suspension is required to increase total travel beyond roughly 9-10.5 inches. [t553]
- Removing sway bars is the easiest way to maximize suspension articulation. [t553]
- Lifting via suspension reduces static droop but increases compression travel. [t553]
- [Partial] Install bumpers and winches before fine-tuning shock settings to ensure proper clearance. [t553]
